notes: 1. CP portal login URL is the bare path https://uat-web.xrportal.in/ ; the KYC form lives at https://uat-web.xrportal.in/kyc (the FS file still shows the legacy https://uat.xrportal.in/kyc host — both resolve to the same CP portal). Auth is Mobile-OTP only (no password). UAT mobile = 8888888888, CP static OTP = 147258 (NOT the Admin/SM 258369). One session lands the CP on /dashboard; the KYC tile is in the left sidebar (Home / KYC / JBP / Leads / Logout).

2. MODULE MEANING (FSD-CORRECTION 2026-05-25): 'KYC Assistance' in the CP portal is the Channel Partner's OWN firm-level self-KYC onboarding (orgName, address, business region, owner, email, phone, pincode, PAN, optional RERA + 3 document slots). It is NOT customer/buyer KYC-on-behalf. There is NO backend endpoint for a CP to submit KYC for a buyer (buyer KYC is a buyer-portal flow). Per FS 1.2, the WINNER-prerequisite, co-applicant ('max 4 applicants'), Aadhaar-front/back and '4 documents per applicant' rules describe the legacy buyer-KYC model and do NOT apply to this page.

3. FORM STRUCTURE (verified live 2026-06-06, visual-memory cp/kyc-assistance INDEX.md): heading 'KYC'; four green-band sections in order — Firm Details (Firm Name orgName*, Firm Address address*, Business Region select*), Contact Details (Growth Partner Owner Name ownerName*, Email ID email*, Phone Number phone*), Additional Details (Pin Code Office officePincode*, PAN Number panNumber*, RERA Number reraNumber — optional), KYC Document Upload (PAN Card, GST, MAHA RERA Certificate — 3 slots), then footer [Cancel] ... [Submit].

4. SUBMIT GATING (critical UX, verified 2026-06-06 — see FS 1.7 Rule 5 / DOC_DRIFT-CP-KYC-003): the Submit button is disabled=true at the DOM level on a fresh/partial form and only becomes enabled once all 8 required fields (orgName, address, Business Region, ownerName, email, phone, officePincode, panNumber) carry non-empty values. reraNumber is optional. Clicking the disabled Submit is a NO-OP — no toast, no inline field error, no navigation. THE FORM DOES NOT RENDER INLINE PER-FIELD VALIDATION ERRORS ON SUBMIT CLICK. Any TC whose expected result references an inline 'X is required' error is marked [VERIFY WITH DEV] and most likely fails against the disabled-button reality.

5. DOCUMENT UPLOADS (verified): 3 slots (PAN Card / GST / MAHA RERA Certificate), each an <input type=file>. NO client-side 'accept' MIME attribute is present (the client does not constrain file type or size — server-side only). Document uploads are NOT required to enable Submit at the UI gate (Submit can enable with text fields filled and zero docs). FS 1.5 / BRD ('all 4 documents mandatory') is the legacy buyer model — does NOT gate this form. Backend mandatory-document enforcement requires product clarification.

6. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] = a disposable UAT record/state/file or user authorisation must be supplied before executing this test. KYC submit/upload WRITES documents and records to LeadSquared + Azure Blob and flips isKycSubmitted on a live registration unit. Per CLAUDE.md Pipeline Discipline rule 7, NO live-portal Submit/Upload/Approve on a fixture without explicit user authorisation. Every submit/upload TC here carries [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] + a mutation-authorisation note and supplies NO invented PII/PAN/RERA/document.

7. [VERIFY WITH DEV] = behaviour not confirmed in BRD/FRD/FS or contradicted between sources; confirm before treating Pass/Fail as authoritative. Used here for: inline-validation-error expecteds (form uses disabled-button gating instead), the customer-notification side effect, and the backend document-mandatory enforcement.

8. KNOWN BACKEND DEFECTS & SECURITY GAPS (documented in FS + cp.controller.js source review — assert as documented behaviour, do NOT log as new bugs): KB-CPK-02 / DOC — POST /api/v1/cp/registration is UNAUTHENTICATED (route sits before router.use(protect)); KB-CPK-09 — the submit handler looks up the user by req.body.phone and ignores req.user, so a logged-in CP-A can overwrite CP-B's KYC by passing CP-B's phone (privilege escalation); KB-CPK-07 — panDoc extractor searches the filename for substring 'pan card' but uploads are prefixed 'pan' (no 'card') so panDoc can read back null; KB-CPK-08 — sequential doc upload has no rollback (orphan partial state on mid-sequence failure); BR-CPK-03/KB-CPK-10 — GET /cp/kyc with NULL prospect_id returns a generic 400; QA-Risk-7 — pincode (Mavis) fetch runs unconditionally even on re-upload, so a pincode-service outage 500s a re-upload; QA-Risk-12 — a fresh JWT is minted on every successful /cp/registration (token-rotation/logging risk); BUG-CPK-03 — the success_registercp WhatsApp template renders '91<phone>' (missing '+').

9. KYC GLOSSARY: 'Self-KYC' = CP firm-level KYC submitted via POST /cp/registration. 'kyc:true' = re-upload flag in the registration body that bypasses the 400 'User already registered' guard (BR-CPK-01) and suppresses the success_registercp WhatsApp. 'Business Region' = MMR (Mumbai Metropolitan Region) / Pune / BGLR (Bengaluru) — the 3 HoABL sales regions, the ONLY options in the select. 'Your KYC is in review' = the navy/shield dashboard-header indicator shown while CP KYC awaits admin approval; it disappears once approved. GET /api/v1/cp/kyc = authenticated read returning { orgName, address, ownerName, email, phone, businessRegion, officePincode, panNumber, reraNumber, reraDoc, panDoc, gstDoc } from LeadSquared.

10. DOC_DRIFT-CP-KYC-001 — BRD §3 Rule 9 and §7 (CP-BRD-CP-Portal.md) still state '4 KYC documents required: Photo, PAN, Aadhaar front, Aadhaar back' with co-applicants (max 4) and a WINNER prerequisite. The LIVE UI and FS-KYC-Assistance.md show 3 firm documents (PAN Card / GST / MAHA RERA Certificate), no co-applicants and no WINNER gate. The FS file already carries the FSD-CORRECTION/DOC_DRIFT annotations and WINS; TCs in this pass use the observed (firm self-KYC, 3-document) model. The legacy buyer-KYC TC IDs (CP_KYC_005,006,011,013,014,017,018,022,024,025,026,027 and CP_KYC_002,003 WINNER-gate) are PRESERVED (never renumbered/deleted) but grouped under 'Deprecated Buyer-KYC Model (superseded)' and flagged — their expecteds describe the deprecated model, not the live form.

11. DOC_DRIFT-CP-KYC-002 — Business Region option set (MMR / Pune / BGLR) confirmed from the live dropdown capture (kyc-business-region-dropdown.png) and recorded in FS 1.4; the older spec did not enumerate options. DOC_DRIFT-CP-KYC-003 — submission is gated by the disabled-Submit pattern, not by click-time inline field errors; legacy TCs asserting inline 'X is required' errors are flagged [VERIFY WITH DEV].

12. PRE-FILL BEHAVIOUR is non-deterministic (visual-memory note): the 2026-06-03 capture showed all fields pre-filled (GP test name / gp@test.test / Test CP / testcp@gmail.com / 8888888888 / 400056 / TTTTT7777Y) while the 2026-06-06 fresh capture showed an EMPTY form for the SAME CP (HV00025808). Hypothesis: the form pre-fills only when the CP's KYC record is in a draft/in-review state. TCs that assert specific pre-filled values are [VERIFY WITH DEV] — confirm the current GET /cp/kyc response before treating exact-value assertions as authoritative.

tcs.scenario: To verify POST /cp/registration is UNAUTHENTICATED (security gap)
tcs.description: Verify the documented critical gap: the CP registration/KYC submit endpoint requires no token.
tcs.precond: An existing CP X with phone P_X, isCpRegistrationCompleted=true. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access + EXPLICIT USER AUTHORISATION (this would overwrite a live CP's KYC).

2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: KNOWN SECURITY GAP (KB-CPK-02): the route sits BEFORE router.use(protect), so the call succeeds with no token — anyone knowing P_X can overwrite CP X's LeadSquared KYC documents. Document and recommend adding auth middleware. (Critical.)

tcs.scenario: To verify a logged-in CP-A can overwrite CP-B's KYC via body phone (privilege escalation)
tcs.description: Verify the documented ownership-check gap where the handler trusts req.body.phone over req.user.
tcs.precond: CP A logged in; CP B has phone P_B. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access for CP A + EXPLICIT USER AUTHORISATION (overwrites CP B's KYC).
tcs.steps:
1. As CP A, POST /api/v1/cp/registration with body phone=P_B, kyc:true and attached docs.
2. Read the response and CP B's KYC state.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] CP A token + P_B + mutation authorisation
tcs.expected: KNOWN BUG (KB-CPK-09, cp.controller.js:42): the controller looks up the user by req.body.phone and ignores req.user, so CP B's KYC is updated by CP A. Document the privilege escalation; recommend deriving the target from req.user. (Critical.)
